old_description: The DySyn Group represents manufacturers of medium-voltage motors, drives, switchgear, breakers, generator docking stations and transformers to the primary power users and electrical utility customers of Northern California and Nevada.
about:
The DySyn Group, LLC is based in North Highlands, California, with a mailing address in Foresthill. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, nor are the names of its founders. It operates as a manufacturer's representative serving the electrical power sector in Northern California and Nevada.

The firm represents manufacturers of medium-voltage motors, drives, switchgear, breakers, generator docking stations, and transformers. It also offers National Breaker Services and is described as an industry leader in power house switchgear and iso-phase bus duct design, manufacturing, and installation, as well as switchgear and circuit breaker life extension for voltages ranging from 480 V to 38 kV.

Its customer base consists of primary power users and electrical utility companies across Northern California and Nevada. The company focuses on the power generation and distribution sector, serving clients that require medium-voltage equipment and switchgear life-extension services.

name: The Electric and Solar Specialist
old_description: "If I could give more stars, I would! My solar works exactly as they described it would and they were extremely professional and followed up to see how everything is doing.  I highly recommend them and will definitely be using them for everything electric and solar!"
about:
The Electric & Solar Specialist opened in 2018 in Cheyenne, Wyoming, as a locally owned and operated electrical and solar contracting firm. The company was established to provide affordable, quality solar installations and electrical services to the region, and it holds a Wyoming solar contractor license.

The firm delivers full-service residential and commercial electrical work, including service upgrades, bucket truck services, pole barn wiring, generator installation, lighting retrofits, and annual maintenance contracts. Its solar division handles design, permitting, installation, and commissioning of photovoltaic systems, often integrating electrical upgrades such as panel replacements or EV charger readiness into the same project.

Customers range from homeowners seeking rooftop solar or hot-tub wiring to businesses undertaking LED lighting retrofits or new construction electrical. The company cites projects such as whole-home solar commissions, commercial panel upgrades, and emergency after-hours service calls as typical engagements.

The owners have said the business was started because Wyoming’s small communities mean repeat encounters with customers, making reputation and workmanship essential. The company emphasizes that its dual electrical and solar licenses allow it to assess and execute projects that single-trade contractors cannot.

name: The Fabric Cobbler
old_description: First and foremost, thank you for being here, in my shop - whether in person or online. Many folks know that my teens and I recently obtained an order protection for ourselves and our pets - it's been a journey. Please know that every purchase is so helpful right now. Going to one income in an economy where I can't dependably pay myself as the owner is rough. We all, from the bottom of our hearts, appreciate the support of my shop.
about:
The Fabric Cobbler operates a retail fabric and craft store in Forsyth, Illinois. The shop has been in business since at least 2007, as indicated by its copyright notice, and is run by the owner alongside her teenage children. The owner describes the venture as a personal endeavor born from a desire to create a welcoming community space.

The store carries a wide range of products including designer fabrics, precut fabric bundles, craft kits, notions, patterns, books, and needlework supplies. It also offers classes and events, as well as community programs such as a guild. The retail space is organized to allow customers to browse extensive fabric collections, and the owner emphasizes a curated selection that includes designs not commonly found in other shops.

The primary customers are individual consumers—quilters, sewists, crafters, and hobbyists—who visit the physical storefront during posted hours (Monday–Tuesday 12 p.m.–7 p.m., Wednesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–4 p.m.). The shop also sells online through its website and engages customers via live auctions on WhatNot and multiple social media channels.

The owner states that the shop was founded to provide a fully inclusive safe space for all people regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, creed, or religion. An intersex- and BIPOC-inclusive flag is displayed in the window, and the owner has taken a public anti-MAGA stance, accepting the loss of some business as a consequence. Customers frequently cite the shop’s organization, unique fabric offerings, and the owner’s personal engagement as reasons for their loyalty.

name: The Iron Works LTD.
old_description: Providing custom metal fabrication services, solutions, and construction steel since 1984.
about:
The Iron Works Ltd. has operated from Des Moines, Iowa since 1984, when Charles Punelli took ownership of the business. Over the ensuing decades the shop has grown into a full-service metal fabrication house serving the central Iowa region and beyond.

The company runs a 22,000-square-foot production facility equipped for MIG/TIG welding, plasma cutting, shearing, press-brake forming, ironworker operations, and overhead crane handling. It specializes in custom-built steel staircases and also produces planters, mailboxes, and one-off prototypes, offering design and development support alongside fabrication. Detailing services and mirror-finish polishing round out the in-house capabilities, and a fleet of private delivery trucks handles on-site logistics.

Customers span construction, architecture, telecommunications, landscaping, and both residential and commercial markets. Concrete examples include ice-protection solutions for broadcast-tower electronics, architectural staircases for building projects, and custom planters for landscape installations.

The firm emphasizes reliability and a willingness to take on jobs that other shops decline, promising to meet deadlines and "do what it takes to make sure the job is done right." Its differentiators include a no-job-too-big-or-small philosophy, dedicated delivery, and high-end finishing such as mirror polishing.

name: The John R. White Company, Inc.
old_description: John R. White and Bunge Announce Strategic Partnership to Scale Soy Protein Solutions for Food Manufacturers. Read More →
about:
The John R. White Company, Inc. is headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama. The business was established in 1947 by John R. White and L.Q. Patton as a specialized supplier of dairy and bakery ingredients. Over the decades it has evolved into a value‑added distributor of bulk dry ingredients with a focus on functional and technical products.

Today the company operates as a value‑add ingredient distributor, offering strategic sourcing, technical consultation, and reliable execution. It represents more than 100 bulk dry ingredient manufacturers and serves over 800 active customers from BRC‑certified facilities, distributing to more than 38 states primarily in the South. Services include formulation support, ingredient optimization, supply chain management, and inventory optimization.

The company serves food manufacturers across categories such as dry blending and milling, meat and poultry, bakery and snack, beverage and premix, pet food, clean label, spices, and dressings, soups and sauces. Its customer base includes procurement and buying teams, business owners and operations leaders, and R&D and technical staff who rely on the firm for ingredient sourcing, cost reduction, and formulation troubleshooting.

Founded on principles of reliability and cost‑competitiveness, the company differentiates itself through a technical sales force that works directly with client R&D and production teams, a total‑cost sourcing methodology, and a four‑pillar philosophy of innovative solutions, exceptional customer service, earning trust, and building community. A strategic partnership with Bunge to scale soy protein solutions further extends its ingredient portfolio.

name: The Joseph Company
old_description: The skill of furniture building was passed down in the Joseph family over 70 years ago. Every piece crafted is like a Joseph family heirloom.
about:
The Joseph Company operates from Houston, Texas, where it was founded in 1990 by the Joseph family. The business traces its furniture-building heritage back more than 70 years, with skills passed down through generations. Today it remains a family-owned workshop dedicated to custom craftsmanship, building each piece in its own shop.

The shop produces custom-built furniture, casegoods, and offers refinishing and restoration services. Every piece is hand-crafted by skilled artisans in the company's Houston facility, allowing close control over design and construction. The operation focuses on one-of-a-kind items rather than volume production, with each project developed collaboratively.

The company works exclusively with the design trade, serving interior designers, architects, and specifiers who require tailored furnishings for residential and commercial projects. Its client base consists of design professionals seeking collaborative development of unique pieces that meet exact specifications.

The Joseph Company emphasizes its multi-generational expertise and the heirloom quality of its work, positioning each project as a collaborative effort that reflects the client's vision while drawing on decades of family knowledge. The firm's differentiator is the combination of heritage craftsmanship and a made-to-order approach.

name: The LYCRA Company - Waynesboro, VA
old_description: fiber when he walked on the moon in 1969. We’ve only gotten better since.
about:
The LYCRA Company operates its global headquarters in Waynesboro, Virginia, where it was founded in 1958. The company invented the original spandex fiber later branded as LYCRA®, which gained historic recognition when Neil Armstrong wore it on the moon in 1969. No ownership details are disclosed.

The company manufactures a portfolio of branded fibers including LYCRA®, COOLMAX®, and THERMOLITE®, with recent additions made from pre‑consumer waste and partially renewable content. Beyond fiber production, it provides technical support for fabric processes such as knitting, weaving, and seamless construction, plus marketing assistance, product sourcing, and a digital platform (LYCRA ONE™) that enables fabric certification and virtual mill showrooms. Specific facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not publicly disclosed.

Its fibers are engineered for a wide range of garment categories: activewear, athleisure, bedding, denim, hosiery, intimates, personal care, ready‑to‑wear, socks, swimwear, and workwear. Customers include textile mills, apparel brands, and ultimately consumers seeking stretch, comfort, and durability.

The company positions itself on three pillars: global fiber consistency across its supply chain, collaborative innovation that pairs its R&D and market insights with mill expertise, and sustainable solutions that deliver recycled and renewable fibers without compromising performance.

name: The Little Potato Company - Potato Processing, Packaging, Distribution
old_description: Coloma Farms in Wisconsin has been around since 1961 and Steve joined on with his family when he graduated from college. He's been growing potatoes for The Little Potato Company since 2016.
about:
The Little Potato Company is headquartered in DeForest, Wisconsin. The company traces its roots to 1996 when Angela and her father started with two shovels, a rented one-acre plot, and a dream in Canada. Canadian owned and operated since 1996, the business expanded to the United States in 2016, establishing American operations in Wisconsin. The company partners with family farms such as Coloma Farms, which has been operating since 1961, and growers like Steve who joined his family farm after college and has supplied the company since 2016.

The company specializes in growing, processing, packaging, and distributing small potato varieties. Working with a network of family farms across Canada and the U.S., it oversees planning, planting, growing, harvesting, and storing practices through its variety development team. The potatoes are packaged into consumer-ready products, including microwave-ready flavored lines such as Savory Herb and garlic and herb, and distributed to retail stores.

The Little Potato Company serves the retail grocery and foodservice sectors, supplying branded potato products to stores across North America. Its customers include busy families seeking convenient, fresh whole-food options, as evidenced by consumer testimonials. The company also partners with retail and office partners for distribution.

The business was built around family values—integrity, reliability, respect, and humility—and aims to create "little moments of happiness" for consumers. Sustainability is a core belief, reflected in responsible farmland use and generational partnerships with farming families.

name: The Millwork Lab
old_description: At The Millwork Lab we take pride in our fine, detailed oriented work from start to finish. Our carpenters are exceptional artisans, capable of creating superior quality architectural millwork, furniture, wall panels and kitchen cabinets for both residential and commercial properties.
about:
The Millwork Lab operates from a shop at 4420 NW 35th Court in Miami, Florida, producing custom architectural millwork, furniture, and cabinetry for residential and commercial projects. No founding year or ownership structure is publicly disclosed.

The company’s capabilities span custom woodwork, veneering with exotic laid veneers, and fabrication of fire-rated and solid-stock cores. Its output includes kitchen cabinets, commercial casework, custom furniture, decorative beams and columns, interior doors, wall and ceiling panels, elevator wood frames, and lobby and reception millwork. The shop emphasizes craftsmanship and machinery to create custom architectural profiles, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed. It works with a variety of wood species and applies finishes ranging from paints to specialized colors and styles.

The Millwork Lab serves architects, interior designers, general contractors, and homeowners across residential and commercial construction. Projects range from luxury home interiors to commercial lobby and reception areas, with the company highlighting its ability to meet client-specified time frames. The firm also offers design collaboration, working with clients or their designers to develop custom solutions.

The firm distinguishes itself through exotic custom laid veneers, a wide selection of woods, finishes, paints, and colors, and the capacity to deliver high-quality custom architectural profiles on schedule. It positions its production capabilities as a step above other woodworking shops in the Miami area.

name: The Neil Jones Food Company
old_description: We are a family-run, privately-owned, U.S. Corporation processing fresh-packed
about:
The Neil Jones Food Company is a family-run, privately-owned U.S. corporation headquartered in Vancouver, Washington. Founded in 1915 as San Benito Foods, the company began with a single can of premium San Benito tomatoes processed fresh from the field. The business has remained under family stewardship, with James Matthew Jones currently serving as CEO.

The company processes fresh-packed Pacific Northwest fruit — including pears, cherries, plums, and cranberries — and California tomato products such as canned tomatoes, pouches, custom sauces, and industrial varieties. It operates three processing facilities strategically located for national and international shipping. The Northwest Packing facility has canned Pacific Northwest fruit and produced industrial juices, purees, and blends since the 1970s. The TomaTek facility, built in the 1980s, specializes in aseptic technology for fresh-pack California tomatoes in industrial sizes and #10 equivalent pouches. All products are made in the U.S.A.

Customers span foodservice, industrial, retail, chain, and international channels. The company serves independent restaurants, school lunch programs, food manufacturers, chain restaurants, healthcare facilities, juice manufacturers, and cruise lines worldwide. Products appear under private label brands and in restaurants across the country.

The company emphasizes sustainable fresh-packing within hours of harvest, working closely with growers and agronomists to ensure quality ingredients. It highlights its commitment to not taking shortcuts, maintaining strict quality standards, and offering extensive customization capabilities for private label and foodservice partners.
